sections.h2: What kind of county is Oglethorpe County?
sections.html:
Oglethorpe County is a rural Piedmont county in northeastern Georgia, with Lexington as its seat, and Wikipedia calls it the largest county in Northeast Georgia. It was founded on December 19, 1793 and named for Georgia's founder, Gen. James Oglethorpe, per Wikipedia. The land was part of a tract the Creek and Cherokee surrendered to the Colony of Georgia in the treaty of 1773.

The county spans 442 square miles, of which 439 are land. Most of it lies in the Broad River sub-basin of the Savannah River basin, and a narrow western strip, running past Woodville, Crawford and Winterville, drains to the Upper Oconee. Seven counties touch it: Elbert, Wilkes, Taliaferro, Greene, Oconee, Clarke and Madison.

The cities are Arnoldsville, Crawford and Lexington, with Maxeys as a town. Philomath, Point Peter, Sandy Cross, Stephens and Vesta are unincorporated. Part of the Oconee National Forest and Watson Mill Bridge State Park fall inside the county, and recreation draws include whitewater rafting on the Broad River, hunting and agritourism among its recreation draws. The county is part of the Athens-Clarke County metropolitan area.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Oglethorpe County?
sections.html:
Oglethorpe County is thinly settled, with 33.8 residents per square mile and a median owner-occupied home value of $231,600 for 2020-2024. Owners occupy 83.8% of housing.

The 2020 census counted 14,825 residents, 5,803 households and a median age of 43.3, and all of the population lived in rural areas. Of 6,343 housing units, 8.5% were vacant. Commuters average 32.8 minutes to work, and 83.6% of households hold a broadband subscription. One K-12 district, the Oglethorpe County School District, serves the whole county.

sections.h2: Where are the Oglethorpe County tax offices?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner works from 339 West Main St. in Lexington, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 305, Lexington, GA 30648. The phone is (706) 743-8422, and the office is open Monday to Friday from 8:00 to 5:00, closing Fridays from noon to 1:00, per its general information page.

  • Tax Commissioner: bills, collections, mobile home decals and liens
  • Tax Assessors, (706) 743-5166: values, exemptions and the appeals process
  • Board of Equalization: appointed by the Grand Jury, hears administrative appeals of assessor values
  • Board of Commissioners and Board of Education: set their own mill rates
  • Clerk of Superior Court, in the courthouse: warranty deeds

The commissioner also acts as agent of the state for vehicle registration. Because the office does not set value or millage, a complaint about either goes to the assessors or the taxing board.

sections.h2: When is Oglethorpe County property tax due?
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property taxes are normally due December 20 each year in Oglethorpe County, per the county's tax FAQ. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1, and motor vehicles follow the owner's birthday.

  • Interest of 1% per month is charged after December 20
  • A 10% penalty applies to tax not paid within 90 days of the deadline, except homesteaded property with a liability under $500
  • Tax unpaid beyond 90 days is subject to a FiFa lien recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court
  • Mobile homes pay a 10% filing penalty plus 1% a month after April 1, and an unpaid home can be sold at auction

Bills are mailed to the homeowner, never to the mortgage company, so forward yours if a lender escrows the tax. The FAQ warns that a recorded FiFa is public, so credit bureaus may use it, and the tax office has no control over them.

sections.h2: Why does Oglethorpe County assess at 40% when a city assesses at 100%?
sections.html:
The county's tax FAQ says Oglethorpe County assesses property at 40% of fair market value, the Georgia standard, but the city assesses at 100%. Ask the tax office or the city clerk which levies and which assessment base apply to your parcel.

The tax commissioner's general information page explains the chain: fair market value is set as of January 1, the assessed value is 40% of it, and the county commission and school board set mill rates. One mill is one dollar per $1,000 of assessed value, and the bill is the net assessed value after exemptions times the millage.

The state revenue commissioner reviews digests so assessment is uniform between counties, and the state levies a small ad valorem tax of its own, capped at one-fourth of one mill.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an Oglethorpe County value or claim homestead?
sections.html:
An owner has 45 days from the date of the assessment notice to appeal, and the grounds can be taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption. The written appeal goes first to the Board of Tax Assessors and must name the chosen method.

Mobile home owners who disagree with a value have 45 days from the date bills are mailed. Someone unhappy with the assessors' decision on that value can appeal to the Board of Equalization within 21 days of the notice. Call the assessors at (706) 743-5166 for forms.

  • Own and occupy the home as of January 1 to qualify for homestead
  • Applications may be submitted any time, but must be received before April 1 to count for that tax year; later ones start the next year
  • Once approved, you need not reapply while you stay in the same house; a move means a new application
  • An additional homestead exemption is available when the owner reaches age 62

sections.h2: What should an Oglethorpe County seller handle before closing?
sections.html:
Start with a written payoff from the Tax Commissioner and a check of the lien record at the Clerk of Superior Court. Tax unpaid beyond 90 days can lead to a FiFa on the docket, and a lien found late in the process can delay a sale.

Gather the warranty deed, which the Clerk's deed room in the Oglethorpe County Courthouse can copy for you. If you are selling a mobile home, check that the current decal is displayed, since the decal is issued when the year's tax is paid and a location permit requires that tax to be paid in full.

A seller who buys elsewhere must reapply for homestead at the new address, as the office states that a move requires a fresh application. The office phone, (706) 743-8422, answers questions about balances and decals.

faqs.q: When is Oglethorpe County property tax due?
faqs.a: December 20 each year for real estate and business personal property, and April 1 for mobile and manufactured homes. Interest of 1% per month starts after December 20.

faqs.q: Is there a late penalty in Oglethorpe County?
faqs.a: Yes. A 10% penalty applies to tax not paid within 90 days of the deadline. Homesteaded property with a liability under $500 is excused from that 90-day penalty.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal an Oglethorpe County assessment?
faqs.a: 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. File in writing with the Board of Tax Assessors and say which method of appeal you want. The assessors' phone number is (706) 743-5166.

faqs.q: Who sets the tax rate in Oglethorpe County?
faqs.a: The county Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education each adopt a mill rate. The Tax Commissioner bills and collects but does not set value or millage.

faqs.q: Which cities are in Oglethorpe County?
faqs.a: Lexington is the county seat, and the other two cities are Arnoldsville and Crawford. Maxeys is a town. The whole county was classed as rural in the 2020 census.
